correctness.rationale: The Lindblad-to-Lyapunov conversion specifies A and D without a hidden stability assumption. Permutation produces two quadratics with strictly positive linear and constant coefficients, hence a Hurwitz drift. The unique stationary covariance is verified directly to be diagonal, with positive thermal symplectic gap. Covariance Taylor coefficients and a local symplectic squeeze show smaller partially transposed symplectic eigenvalue \(1/2-g\Omega t^2/2+O(t^3)\), proving immediate entanglement. Spectral continuity at the mixed, separable stationary product proves the existence of an eventual time after which it is separable forever. Reproducibility tests include independent ODE integration and finite-Fock Lindblad evolution but are not substituted for analytic proof.

value.rationale: The same physically motivated device exhibits provable immediate entanglement generation and exact loss of all intermode information despite persistent stored energy. This resolves the sharp qualitative contrast between transient quantum correlations and a coupling-independent asymptotic product state. The universal quadratic onset coefficient and permanent late-time separability statement give genuinely non-marginal information beyond previously computed holder-energy curves; no general theorem of arbitrary optical devices is claimed.
